title: States Weekly: August 26, 2026
text:
States Weekly: August 26, 2026

Newsletter
by

Aryan D’Rozario

Published August 26, 2026

Big News: Assam unveils a Hydrocarbon Exploration, Production and Upstream Ecosystem Development Policy, 2026; Maharashtra amends the Maharashtra Government Rules of Business; Andhra Pradesh passes Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Fourth Amendment) Bill 2026; Karnataka passes the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Bill; Assam approves Assam Industrial Relation Rules, 2026; The Union government notifies the Master Plan of Delhi 2047 (MPD-2047); and more.Health Maharashtra announces a new training policy for its Public Health Department (PHD). The policy aims to strengthen the skills of healthcare professionals employed by the PHD and improve the quality of public healthcare services.Source: Mid-dayAndhra Pradesh approves the Transplantation of Human Organs (Amendment) Bill, 2026. It expands the list of recognized close relatives eligible to donate organs (adding grandparents and maternal uncles and aunts), permits swap donation between incompatible donor-recipient pairs, and sets stringent penalties for illegal organ removal and trade.Source: The PrintTamil Nadu amends its maternity leave policy for women government employees. Under the new policy, these employees will be eligible for 365 days of leave for a third child, matching the benefit already offered for the first two.Source: Times of IndiaTamil Nadu announces an increase in annual coverage under the state's Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme. The annual sum will be increased to $26,123 (INR 25 lakh) from $5,224 (INR 5 lakh).Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Press Release (in Tamil)Goa declares cancer a “notifiable disease.” Authorities must now be notified of any new diagnosis of cancer by healthcare providers or laboratories.Source: The PrintAssam approves the Assam Private Coaching Institutes (Control and Student Mental Health Safeguard) Rules, 2026. It aims to bring the growing number of coaching centers in the state under a regulatory framework focused on students’ mental health, safety, and academic concerns.Source: Assam TribuneIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsClimate Change and EnergyDelhi announces a phased shift towards cleaner light goods vehicles (LGVs). Under the new policy, only electric N1 light goods vehicles (with a maximum mass not exceeding 7,716 pounds/ or 3.5 tons) will be allowed to be registered in Delhi from January 1, 2027. In the wider National Capital Region (NCR), the rule will be enforced from July 1, 2027.Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Notification, Press ReleaseKarnataka issues Draft KERC (Electricity Supply) Regulations, 2026. The regulations issued by the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) seek to create a uniform set of rules for consumers and distribution licensees across Karnataka.Source: Solar QuarterIn detail: Draft Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (Electricity Supply) Regulations, 2026Rajasthan mandates planting trees for renewable energy projects approvals. It requires solar, wind, hybrid projects and associated infrastructure such as transmission corridors to include plans for afforestation and green cover measures into project design and long-term land management plans.Source: Construction WorldTamil Nadu announces a simplified procedure for new domestic electricity connections. Single-phase domestic connections not requiring an extension or improvement works will be sanctioned based on “self-declaration,” without a field inspection.Source: DT NextAssam unveils a Hydrocarbon Exploration, Production and Upstream Ecosystem Development Policy, 2026. It aims to boost exploration of oil and natural gas across Assam, particularly in areas where hydrocarbons have not yet been discovered.Source: North East TodayIn detail: NotificationJammu and Kashmir approves a 6.83 percent average increase in electricity tariffs for FY 2026-27. The revised tariff, issued by the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, will come into effect from September 1, 2026.Source: ETVIn detail: JERC orderLadakh approves a 6.83 percent average increase in electricity tariffs for FY 2026-27. The revised tariff, issued by the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, will come into effect from September 1, 2026.Source: ETVIn detail: JERC orderTripura announces a 100 percent subsidy on electricity tariffs. The state will bear the entire electricity tariff hike effective retrospectively from May 2026.Source: Ukhrul TimesIn detail: Press releaseUttarakhand issues Draft UERC (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2026. The regulations issued by the Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory Commission (UERC) aim at strengthening grid discipline, operational security, and financial accountability across Uttarakhand.Source: Solar QuarterIn detail: Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory Commission (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2026FinanceNothing critical to report this week.Industrial Policy and Business RegulationsHaryana notifies the Diesel Generator Set Subsidy Scheme. Under the scheme, 50 percent of the cost of a generator, up to $23,800 (INR 20 lakh), will be reimbursed to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) for the purchase of new generator sets. The state's MSMEs will be eligible for a 50 percent reimbursement of the cost of Retrofit Emission Control Devices (RECD), subject to a maximum of $5,950 (INR 5 lakh).Source: TribuneIn Detail: Haryana Diesel Generator Set Subsidy SchemeRajasthan issues Rajasthan Value Added Tax Rules, 2026. The rules lay down a comprehensive procedural and digital compliance framework for the administration of Value Added Tax under the Rajasthan Value Added Tax Act, 2025.Source: A2Z TaxcorpIn detail: Rajasthan Value Added Tax (Amendment) Rules, 2026Himachal Pradesh extends the Himachal Pradesh Industrial Investment Policy, 2019. The 2019 policy expired on December 31, 2025, but was first extended till March 31, 2026, and now has once again been granted a two-month extension from August 12, 2026, to October 12, 2026.Source: The TribuneIn detail: NotificationAndhra Pradesh passes The Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026. It aims to simplify regulations, ease approval procedures and build a more investor-friendly, trust-based regulatory system, including an auto-appeal mechanism for delayed public services, revamped fire-safety audit rules, and a two-tier committee system to fast-track industrial clearances.Source: Deccan ChronicleLand Acquisition and Labor RegulationsMaharashtra lifts freeze on the allotment of state-owned land to cooperative housing societies, imposed since 2010. Under the revised policy, cooperative societies will have to reserve 20 percent of their housing space for backward-classes and an additional 5 percent for disabled persons.Source: Economic TimesJammu and Kashmir notifies its Land Pooling Policy, 2026. The policy mandates any developer or consortium to secure “voluntary consent” from at least 70 percent of the landowners in a contiguous area before proceeding with land pooling schemes.Source: JK OneIn detail: Jammu and Kashmir Land Pooling Policy 2026Assam approves the Assam Industrial Relation Rules, 2026. The rules are based on the Union government’s Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and replace three colonial-era and post-independence regulations to streamline state labor governance.Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsAssam approves the Assam Social Security Rules, 2026. Framed under the Union government's Code on Social Security, 2020, it aims to modernize the labor ecosystem and make it more efficient and worker centric.Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsInfrastructure and GovernanceMaharashtra amends the Maharashtra Government Rules of Business. It empowers the Chief Minister of Maharashtra to override decisions made by any Minister, provided the action is deemed to in the public interest and the reasons are recorded in writingSource: NDTVIn detail: Maharashtra Government Rules of Business (Fourth Amendment Rules), 2026Andhra Pradesh passes the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2026. It restores direct elections for mayors and municipal chairpersons, replacing the current indirect election system.Source: Deccan ChronicleAndhra Pradesh passes the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026. It links property registration with municipal mutation records allowing the name of the owner to automatically update in municipal records at the time of registration, instead of requiring a separate mutation process afterward.Source: Deccan ChronicleAndhra Pradesh passes the Payment of Salaries and Pension and Removal of Disqualifications (Amendment) Bill, 2026. It amends the 1953 Act governing salaries, allowances and pensions of ministers, legislators, and holders of specified legislative offices.Source: Deccan ChronicleAndhra Pradesh passes the Panchayat Raj (Second Amendment) Bill, 2026. It abolishes the posts of second vice-president in ‘Mandal Praja Parishads’ (Sub-District People’s Councils; MPPs) and second vice-chairperson in ‘Zilla Praja Parishads’ (District People’s Councils; ZPPs).Source: Deccan ChronicleAndhra Pradesh approves 34 percent reservation for Backward Classes (BCs) in Rural Local Bodies and 33.1 percent in Urban Local Bodies.Source: The South FirstIn detail: OrderGujarat increases the maximum annual family income limit for students from unreserved categories seeking assistance under its Foreign Study Loan Scheme. The limit increases from $6, 269 to $10,500 (INR 6 lakh to 10 lakh). The decision aims to make more students from middle-income families eligible for loan assistance for pursuing higher education abroad.Source: Economic TimesKarnataka passes the Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2026. The bill aims to provide a clear legal framework for the governance, management, and use of common areas and facilities in apartment buildings. It also deals with the ownership of an individual apartment and undivided shares and interest in common areas and facilities.Source: Deccan ChronicleIn detail: Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2026Karnataka passes the Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The bills aim to provide a legal mechanism for dealing with roads and drains in unauthorized layouts and converting eligible properties from “B-Khata” (properties in unauthorized layouts) to “A-Khata” (properties that comply with all regulations). The bills apply to Municipal Corporations (for larger cities) and Municipalities (smaller cities and towns).Source: Deccan ChronicleIn detail: Karnataka Municipalities (Amendment) Bill, 2026, Karnataka Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Bill, 2026Karnataka amends the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975. The amendment bill sanctions the government to use a portion of parks (up to 5 percent) for infrastructure projectsSource: Deccan HeraldIn detail: Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026Assam approves the creation of eight new co-districts with its headquarters at a central location. The locations will be identified by District Commissioners. With 39 co-districts already operational, the eight new ones will bring the total to 47.Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsAssam approves Assam State Child Protection Policy, 2026. It aims to ensure the safety, security, dignity and wellbeing of children and serves as a commitment towards effective implementation of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and POCSO Rules, 2020.Source: Economic TimesIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsOdisha launches the ‘Bidesh Sikhyabruti’ (Foreign Education) Scholarship Scheme. It aims to support Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) students seeking higher education at top global universities. Each recipient will receive financial assistance of up to $26,123 (INR 25 lakh) per annum, covering tuition fees, accommodation, living expenses, international travel, medical insurance and other incidental costs.Source: The TelegraphIn detail: Guidelines – BideshSikhyabrutiWater and SanitationHaryana announces revised compensation structure for sanitation workers. Under the updated framework, sanitation workers currently drawing a total remuneration of $215 (INR 20,590) per month will see an increase to $236 (INR 22,590).Source: ANICenter – State Relations The Union government notifies the Master Plan of Delhi 2047 (MPD-2047). It allows for high-rise and high-density development in the National Capital.Source: Hindustan TimesIn detail: Master Plan for Delhi 2047The Union government approves the establishment of a bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh in the Union Territory of Ladakh.Source: India TodayIn detail: Press Information Bureau, DelhiAny OtherBihar amends the Bihar Social-Media and Other Online Media Rules, 2026. Social media creators producing content on Bihar government schemes and programs can earn up to $1045 (INR 1 lakh) per video.Source: Indian ExpressIn detail: Cabinet DecisionsMaharashtra issues a statewide 14-clause compliance and enforcement order for the edible oil industry. The order mandates sale only in “sealed, tamper-evident and fully labelled packages”, prohibiting loose or unpackaged oil.Source: Times of India
